newsitem.title: USA: Ford to unveil new Mercury concept car Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Ford to unveil new Mercury concept car Tuesday.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. is scheduled to introduce a new Mercury concept car Tuesday, which analysts said will be a smaller replacement for the mid-sized Mercury Cougar coupe now being phased out.

The new vehicle will be a stylish, front-wheel-drive coupe built off the Mondeo platform that incorporates "new-edge" design looks, according to analysts. It will not carry the Cougar name, although Ford officials have said the Cougar nameplate has not been permanently retired.

"This is part of a strategy to try to provide Lincoln-Mercury, and especially Mercury, with its own exclusive product line," said Christopher Cedergren, managing director of Nextrend, a Thousand Oaks, Calif., consulting firm. Lincoln-Mercury spokeswoman Anne Doyle said the vehicle will be the third concept car that Mercury has introduced this year. That makes it the first time in several years that Mercury, which has struggled to find a clear market identity, has unveiled so many new concept products in one year.
Doyle said Mercury plans a national image advertising campaign this fall to highlight what Ford considers to be the brands' attributes of fun, flexibility and flair.

The U.S. No. 2 automaker has been laying the groundwork for such a move since January, when Mercury unveiled the MC4 concept car at the North American Auto Show in Detroit. Designed as a coupe, the crisp-looking MC4 has two extra side doors, an integrated child seat, adjustable pedals, telescoping instrument dials and a trunk with two "gull-wing" lids.
Mercury also showed the L'Attitude, a hybrid between a Sable station wagon and sport utility vehicle.

Mercury plans to start production of the new coupe at Ford's AutoAlliance joint venture with Mazda Motor Corp. in Flat Rock, Mich., in August, said Cedergren. The vehicle is slated to go on sale in October 1998 as a 1999 model.

The new car will be more than 1 foot shorter than the rear-wheel-drive Cougar it replaces, said Cedergren. Even though coupe sales have been declining, he said the remaining growth in the segment is in the smaller models.

Cedergren said the new Mercury car will be more similar in size to the redesigned Accord coupe that Honda Motor Co. Ltd. plans to introduce later this year, and the Solara coupe from Toyota Motor Co., due out next summer.
He added that Ford will sell a version of the new vehicle in Europe as the Ford Probe.

Ford announced in March the Cougar would be discontinued as part of a plan to kill off four slow-selling vehicles. Also being phased out are the Cougar's Ford twin, the Thunderbird, the Probe sports coupe and the Aerostar rear-wheel-drive minivan.
The Cougar and Thunderbird were previously made at Ford's assembly plant in Lorain, Ohio.
